One absurdly long 30-story apartment wall with six connected sections bending slightly into a shallow zigzag. Cream concrete with dusty apricot patches and dark blue glazed balcony columns; unrelenting dense rhythmic window rows. Single tiny entrance canopy and a microscopic red-yellow playground at its foot make the wall look ridiculously overpopulated.

One enormous U-shaped 30-story residential megablock enclosing a comically tiny courtyard. Three connected tall walls; front is open toward viewer so narrow deep courtyard remains visible, no foreground wall hiding it. Pale gray and dirty beige facades, dense dark blue vertical glazed balcony strips, tiny orange playground stranded at bottom. This is an inhabited ordinary Russian economy housing complex, oppressive scale rendered as cute miniature.

Three extremely tall boxy 33-story mass-market PIK-inspired apartment towers packed closely on a single tiny ground slab. Modern flat facade grids with no protruding balconies; huge geometric blocks of muted terracotta, mustard and off-white, dark gray flat roofs. Towers of slightly different heights, staggered so all three read clearly, hundreds of tiny identical square windows. Dwarf them with a single minute sapling and playground below. Recognizable Salarevo Park-inspired anonymous commodity housing.

A tightly clustered comb-shaped residential complex: three monotonous parallel 30-story apartment slabs attached at their far ends by one lower crossbar. Each slab slender and very tall, staggered to expose repeated facades and narrow gaps; white and cold light gray with pale powder-blue panel strips and deep navy vertical glazed loggias. Ridiculously tiny paved inner passage and a single little lawn. Samolet Moscow-region mass-market architecture inflated into an absurd 30-story repetitive megacomplex, not a literal replica.

A single immense stepped apartment megastructure made of five connected slab sections rising in a staircase from 20 to 35 floors, like a gigantic concrete organ. Dense repetitive windows and strong vertical enclosed glass balcony bands. Off-white, desaturated blue-gray, and dull teal facade patches, flat gray roofs at different levels. Building width roughly equals height. A comically microscopic orange swing at the base reveals the scale. Recognizable Murino / New Moscow economy-class human anthill, physically plausible but grotesquely oversized.
